core_obligations: Reduce to a morphism of finite presentation: the question is local on X and S, so take X = Spec(B), S = Spec(A) and write B as a quotient of A[x_1, ..., x_n] to get a closed immersion i : X -> A^n_S over S with i_*F finite type and flat at t = i(x) over S; check that the weakly associated point condition and the associated point condition of the fibre are both preserved by i, so it suffices to treat X = A^n_S (proof lines 4001-4022).

Reduce to a finite presentation flat sheaf: choose an elementary etale neighbourhood e : (S', s') -> (S, s) and an open V of X times_S Spec(O_{S', s'}) as in the local structure proposition, let x' be the unique point over x and s', and use the etale up and down lemma to move the statement to X' -> S' with the pullbacks of F and G; then note that the local rings and the stalks of the pullbacks at v and at the closed point agree with those at x' and s', so the statement may be replaced by the one for V -> Spec(O_{S', s'}) (proof lines 4024-4049).

Finish: with f of finite presentation and F of finite presentation and flat over S, shrink X and S to affine neighbourhoods of x and s and apply the finite presentation statement (proof lines 4051-4056).
proof_roadmap: Embed locally into an affine space over the base to make the morphism of finite presentation (proof lines 4001-4022).
Use the local structure proposition and the etale up and down lemma to make the sheaf of finite presentation and flat (proof lines 4024-4049).
Reduce to affine neighbourhoods and invoke the finite presentation statement (proof lines 4051-4056).
difficulty_reason: The lemma generalises the weak Bourbaki statement to a morphism only locally of finite type: for a finite type sheaf F flat at x over S, the point x is weakly associated to F tensor the pullback of G exactly when s is weakly associated to G and x is associated to the fibre of F (statement lines 3983-3998, tag 05IH). The proof is a three stage reduction with real content: a local closed immersion into an affine space over the base making the morphism of finite presentation, then the local structure proposition together with the etale up and down lemma to make the sheaf of finite presentation and flat, and finally the affine reduction to the finite presentation statement. The two reduction steps are the substance, so the claim is H2.
